newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica platinum stocks fuelled by PGM price surge.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica platinum stocks fuelled by PGM price surge.

text.p: Surging platinum and palladium prices fuelled South African platinum stocks on Wednesday, dealers said.
Implats rushed more than five percent higher by 0814 GMT to 50 rand a share and PP Rust climbed nearly five percent to 28 rand a share.
"It's all on the back of the platinum and palladium prices," one dealer said.
Platinum group metals (PGMs) were sharply higher on continued nervousness about when Russian deliveries would start.
Palladium prices zoomed up in early European trade on Wednesday. The metal was last bid at $210 an ounce from its Tuesday London close of $193.00/$197.00 an ounce.
Platinum was last bid at $420 an ounce from a $415.00/$419.00 Tuesday close in London.
South Africa's biggest platinum mine Rusplats added 125 cents to 73.75 rand and Amplats rose 60 cents to 31 rand. Lebowa climbed eight cents to 300 cents.
Struggling Northam was up 10 cents at 226 cents.
